question_text: A steel contains $55 \% \alpha$ and $45 \% \gamma$ at $750^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Estimate the carbon content of the steel. Give your answer as the value of carbon_content_percent.The unit of the answer is %.
response:
## Reasoning

At 750°C, the steel lies in the **α + γ (ferrite + austenite) two-phase region** of the Fe–C diagram. I apply the **lever rule** using the phase-boundary compositions at that temperature.

**Phase boundaries at 750°C** (estimated from the Fe–C diagram):

| Boundary | Endpoints | Composition at 750°C |
|---|---|---|
| Ferrite solvus (α side) | (912°C, 0%) – (727°C, 0.022%) | C_α ≈ 0.017% |
| A₃ line (γ side) | (912°C, 0%) – (727°C, 0.77%) | C_γ ≈ 0.59% |

(Using a √C relation calibrated to the eutectoid point, which matches the curvature of the A₃ line better than a linear fit.)

**Lever rule:**

$$f_\alpha = \frac{C_\gamma - C_0}{C_\gamma - C_\alpha} = 0.55, \qquad f_\gamma = \frac{C_0 - C_\alpha}{C_\gamma - C_\alpha} = 0.45$$

Solving for the overall carbon content:

$$C_0 = f_\alpha\, C_\alpha + f_\gamma\, C_\gamma = 0.55(0.017) + 0.45(0.590) \approx 0.275\;\text{wt\% C}$$

Verification: with C₀ = 0.275, the fractions reproduce 55% α / 45% γ exactly.

$$\boxed{0.27}$$
